redesigned_cot:
APPROACH CHOSEN (of 3 considered). Approach A 'compute true k once, skip median' — REJECTED: changes the boxed value (different k path) so it breaks oracle parity and is unverifiable offline. Approach B 'keep exact arithmetic, only fix the median selection + anchor the silent transforms' — CHOSEN: provably preserves the box byte-for-byte (validated 1597/1597) while removing the only regime-(3) slot and both silent transforms; pure R win, zero oracle risk. Approach C 'shorten division ladder to fewer digits' — REJECTED: changes k strings -> changes box -> breaks oracle; also violates R3 (merging micro-steps). So the redesign = Approach B: same long-mult/long-div/median ARITHMETIC (identical primitives from store_types.py, identical truncation), restructured surface so every committed token is a copy of an earlier printed token.

EXACT RIGID SKELETON (one helper formats every line byte-identically; full range, no skipped indices; no prose in compute region):

LINE 1 (fixed intro): `We use d = k*t^2. I will find k from each example, take the median k, then compute d for the target t.`
LINE 2 (fixed): `I will put my final answer inside \boxed{}.`
LINE 3: blank.

PER EXAMPLE i = 1..N (rigid block, ALWAYS same shape, no optional lines):
  `Example {i}: t = {t_i}, d = {d_i}.`            <- ANCHOR: restate the pair verbatim immediately before use (R2)
  `t^2 = {t_i} * {t_i}:`
  <long_multiplication_lines(t_i,t_i)>            <- one place-value product per line, then running-sum lines (R3, unchanged primitive)
  `= {t_sq_full}`                                  <- ALWAYS emit this result anchor (remove the `if sq_result!=...` conditional; fixes the optional-block leak R3/R5)
  `k = d / t^2 = {d_dp} / {t_sq_full} = {d_cast} / {tsq_cast}:`   <- operands restated on the same line right before the ladder (R2)
  <long_division_lines(d_cast,tsq_cast)>          <- the `= acc + scale*rem/den` ladder, one digit per line (R3, unchanged primitive)
  `k{i} = {k_str}`                                 <- UNIQUE INDEXED ANCHOR for this example's k (replaces the bare `= 2.916`; gives the sort/median step a local copy target)
  blank.

MEDIAN BLOCK (the core R fix — converts the selection into a copy ladder):
  `Collected k values: {k1, k2, ..., kN}`          <- copies each k{i} anchor printed just above
  `Sorted ascending: {s1, s2, ..., sN}`            <- the sorted list (the sort key is the float value; deterministic, no ties matter because values are listed)
  `rank 1: {s1}` / `rank 2: {s2}` / ... / `rank N: {sN}`   <- ONE rank per line, each a pure copy from the sorted list (R3 one-fact-per-line). This is the mechanical spelled-out selection (R4).
  EVEN N: `Count = {N} (even). Lower-middle rank = {N}/2 = {N//2}.`   <- explicit local arithmetic, fixed tie-break direction = lower-middle (R4 fixed tie-break)
  ODD  N: `Count = {N} (odd). Middle rank = ({N}+1)/2 = {N//2+1}.`
  `Median k = value at rank {mid_rank} = {k_fit}.`  <- k_fit is a COPY of the `rank {mid_rank}: {k_fit}` line 1-2 lines above (regime-1 copy, H~0)
  `k = {k_display}.`                                 <- EXPLICIT trailing-zero-strip step shown as its own line; k_display = k_fit.rstrip('0').rstrip('.') (fixes silent transform R2). For the common case k_display==k_fit it is a pure copy; for the 146 strip cases the strip is now VISIBLE on its own line.
  blank.

TARGET BLOCK:
  `Target: t = {q}.`                                <- ANCHOR the target t
  `t^2 = {q} * {q}:`
  <long_multiplication_lines(q,q)>
  `= {t_sq_q}`
  blank.
  `d = k * t^2 = {k_display} * {t_sq_q}:`            <- both operands restated verbatim on the line right before the multiply (R2). k_display copies the `k = {k_display}.` line; t_sq_q copies the `= {t_sq_q}` line.
  <long_multiplication_lines(k_display,t_sq_q)>     <- one place-value product per line + running sums (R3)
  `= {box}`                                          <- box = product truncated at dot+4 (3dp), assembled on a visible line
  blank.
  `The answer is \boxed{{{box}}}`                    <- \boxed content is a character-for-character copy of the `= {box}` line directly above (R6).

Why this is max-R: the ONLY former regime-(3) token (the median pick) is now a copy of a `rank k:` line; the count/middle-rank are explicit single-digit local arithmetic; the trailing-zero strip is a visible line; the final multiply operands are restated immediately above; the box copies the line above. Every committed/derived token is now a deterministic function of a token already printed verbatim earlier in the same completion. Format is one rigid template per block, no optional lines.
oracle_preservation_argument: The redesign reuses the IDENTICAL arithmetic path as the current reasoner: same long_multiplication_lines, same long_division_lines (same 3dp truncation), same sort, same even/odd tie-break (lower-middle for even = len//2-1, middle for odd = len//2), same trailing-zero strip for k_display, same final-product truncation at dot+4. Only the SURFACE LAYOUT changes (added/indexed anchors, an explicit rank ladder, an explicit strip line). Therefore the boxed value is unchanged. I PROVED this offline: I reimplemented the box-value computation independently and, separately, the full redesigned CoT generator, then ran both against the current reasoning_gravity() box and the corpus.jsonl answer on ALL 1597 local gravity problems: box parity 1597/1597 (redesign box == current reasoner box byte-for-byte), grader pass 1597/1597 (rel_tol=1e-2 vs corpus answer), byte-determinism 1597/1597 (two runs identical). Because corpus.py sets final_answer = extract_answer(cot) (self-consistent box) and the box content equals the trace's own `= {box}` line, the grader scores the same value it does today. Oracle (offline solve-rate) is mathematically unchanged.
offline_validation: Reproducible script at /tmp/gravity_redesign_check.py (run from /Users/yimingwang/Kaggle/reason with `python3 /tmp/gravity_redesign_check.py`): it (1) parses examples+target from each decoded prompt in corpus/*/synthetic.jsonl (tokenizer src/tokenizer.json), (2) generates the redesigned CoT twice and the current-reasoner box, (3) asserts redesign-box == current-box (oracle parity), redesign run1 == run2 (determinism), grader rel_tol=1e-2 pass vs corpus.jsonl answer, and (4) tokenizes each redesigned completion to confirm <= 7680. RESULT on all 1597 gravity items: parity 1597/1597, deterministic 1597/1597, grader_ok 1597/1597, max tokens 6230, over-cap 0. To re-run before a paid submission: regenerate the corpus with the new template, then additionally grep the emitted synthetic text for global-rule phrases ('the rule', 'pattern is', 'formula is', 'secret') expecting zero hits, and diff several traces to confirm only literal slot values differ (R5 format-identity).

verdict_fixes.counterexample: none found after honest effort. I reimplemented the full redesigned CoT exactly per the literal skeleton and compared its extracted box to the current reasoner box on ALL 1597 train + 319 holdout + 1278 train_split gravity problems: parity = 0 failures, grader (rel_tol 1e-2 vs corpus answer) = 0 failures, internal '= {box}' vs \boxed{} consistency = 0 failures. I also stress-tested distribution-shift synthetics (3-decimal questions, integer-stripping k_display, magnitude-10 questions, distinct even-N, k_display->integer) and the trickiest real cases (the 146 trailing-zero-strip items e.g. 037c45c6 median 3.950->k_display 3.95->box 43.276; the 67 example blocks where rounded t_sq_full '9.0' != exact mult '9.00'; the 1473 tie cases). Every one matched the current box. The even/odd tie-break written into the trace resolves to the identical sorted index as the code (even -> paired[N//2-1], odd -> paired[N//2]); the degenerate '0'->'' rstrip cannot fire (min real k = 2.452, and it is inherited from the existing reasoner regardless). No instance boxes a wrong answer.
verdict_fixes.fix_if_needed: Oracle is preserved, so no fix is required for correctness. Two optional hardening notes (R-side, not oracle): (1) Drop or correct the 'no ties matter' claim and de-risk the rank-ladder ambiguity by tagging each rank line with its source index (e.g. 'rank {r} (k{src}): {s}') so tied lines are distinguishable to greedy and the median copy target is unique even under duplicate float values. (2) Since 1473/1597 items have duplicate k floats, consider that the sort is stable on the original k_str order (sorted(zip(float,str)) breaks ties lexicographically by string, NOT by example order) - confirm the rank ladder the model is trained to copy uses the SAME stable order the box computation uses (it does in the current parity test, but the augmenter drill for the 'sorted-list -> rank-ladder -> median' primitive should reproduce that exact lexicographic-on-string tie order to avoid teaching a different ordering).
rubric_violations: R4/oracle-irrelevant: the redesign claims 'no ties matter because values are listed', but 1473/1597 real problems have DUPLICATE k float values; the sort tie-break (by k_str) does matter for which rank line a greedy model copies. It happens to be box-safe (equal floats truncate to identical 3dp strings, so 0 cases change k_display), but the stated justification is false and the rank ladder is genuinely ambiguous to a greedy decoder among tied lines -> a real R risk, not the claimed clean copy.

R9/audit-scope: the offline_validation grep targets phrases like 'the rule/pattern/formula is' which never appeared in gravity anyway; the eliminated 'The median k is' slot is replaced by an explicit rank ladder, but the audit does not flag the residual tie-ambiguity in the 'rank k:' ladder as a context-divergent-gold prefix (multiple equal-valued rank lines after a near-identical sorted-list prefix).

verdict_fixes.counterexample: EVEN-COUNT item (verified live, n=4): Collected k values: 4.059, 4.059, 4.060, 4.058 -> Sorted ascending: 4.058, 4.059, 4.059, 4.060. The model must reorder near-equal/duplicate values (4.059 appears twice; gaps <0.002) with the float sort-key not on the page. If greedy mis-binds the sorted order to a train-modal permutation, e.g. emits `Sorted ascending: 4.058, 4.060, 4.059, 4.059`, then `rank 2: 4.060`, and the downstream `Median k = value at rank 2 = 4.060` faithfully copies the WRONG value, propagating to `k = 4.060`, the final multiply `d = 4.060 * 11.0889`, and a boxed answer ~45.020 instead of 45.009 -- a wrong box that the trace still self-consistently supports. This is exactly the 0.95->0.2 propagation pattern: one regime-(3) commit (the sort) cascades through all later copies. (Mitigant: this same sort line exists in the current reasoner, so it is a preserved risk, not introduced; and the redesign removes a strictly worse compounding bare-selection slot.)
verdict_fixes.fix_if_needed: Eliminate the inferred-permutation `Sorted ascending` step so the order becomes a deterministic function of PRINTED tokens. Two oracle-preserving options (both verified to leave the chosen median STRING, hence the box, byte-identical -> oracle stays 1597/1597): (1) SPELL OUT the sort as a mechanical selection-sort ladder (R4): repeatedly emit explicit pairwise comparisons over the collected list to pick `min so far`, one pick per line, each value a copy from the collected line and each ordering decision a visible `a < b` comparison -- turns the permutation into local comparisons. (2) ANNOTATE each k with a printed tie-break key (e.g. its example index or full-precision float) on the collected line, then sort by that VISIBLE key, so the order is a copy/comparison of on-page tokens rather than an in-weights inference. Prefer option (1) (pure R4 mechanical-selection, no extra numeric surface). Also delete the dead `if sqres!=tsqf` branch (emit the `= {tsqf}` anchor unconditionally). After either fix, re-run /tmp/gravity_redesign_check.py to reconfirm box-parity/determinism/grader/cap, and grep the emitted text for zero global-rule phrases. Note: if a paid run is constrained to ONE structural variable, shipping the proposal AS-IS is still a net locality improvement over the current reasoner (it removes the bare selection); the sort fix can be the next single-variable iteration.
rubric_violations: R1/R4 (residual, under-weighted by proposal): the `Sorted ascending: s1, ..., sN` line is an INFERRED PERMUTATION of the `Collected k values:` line, not a verbatim copy of any earlier token. The k values are near-equal noisy estimates of g/2 (verified: 92.2% of items have duplicate k-strings, 99.8% have near-ties <0.002, and the sort actually reorders in 70.3% of items), and the full-precision float sort key used to break ties is NEVER printed. After the identical prefix `Collected k values: <near-equal list>\nSorted ascending: ` many different gold permutations occur across training -> multimodal continuation -> the classic regime-(3) split. NOT defended by value-robustness: a single adjacent transposition in this line changes the chosen median STRING (and thus the box) in 63.2% of items (1009/1597 verified). The proposal dismisses this as 'no ties matter because values are listed', which is incorrect.

R3/R5 (cosmetic, non-blocking): the validated script keeps a vestigial dead `if sqres!=tsqf` branch whose two arms emit the IDENTICAL `= {tsqf}` line. Behavior is uniform (the result anchor is always present, as the prose claims), but the dead conditional should be deleted so the generator literally has no example-block branch (R5 format-identity hygiene).

R6 (minor, preserved/non-blocking): the `= {box}` line is a prefix-copy of the full product that must STOP after exactly 3 decimal places; the stop-point is a fixed truncate-to-3dp rule, not a copied token (verified: full product has >3 frac digits in 1596/1597 items, so a cut is essentially always required). This is a recurring regime-(2) local-derive, is preserved identically from the current reasoner (gravity.py L80-82 `mult_result[:dot+4]`), and is absorbed by the rel_tol=1e-2 grader; flagged for completeness only.
